extracted.intended_audience: federal agency standards executives, program managers, and policy staff responsible for standards participation and OMB Circular A-119 reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting requirements for federal agencies on participation in voluntary consensus standards bodies, use/adoption of voluntary standards, and internal standards-management policies consistent with OMB Circular A-119 and P.L. 104-113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of voluntary consensus standards bodies and agency employees participating
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of voluntary consensus standards bodies in which there is agency participation, as well as the number of agency employees participating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must report counts (example entries in the report list number of standards bodies and number of personnel participating). This is a basic metric for measuring agency engagement with standards bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of voluntary consensus standards the agency has used
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of voluntary consensus standards the agency has used since October 1, 1996 (or those based on procedures in Section 8 of the proposed revision to the Circular).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report total adopted-for-use counts (examples: FDA reported 72, DOE reported 809, DOI 205). This tracks extent of standards utilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of substituted voluntary standards for government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of voluntary consensus standards that have been substituted for government-unique standards as a result of an agency review of existing standards (or as outlined under paragraph 7.c(6) of the proposed revision of the Circular).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should explicitly list any government-unique standards replaced by voluntary standards as a result of review; many agencies reported '0' when none were substituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of effectiveness of Section 7 guidelines and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: An evaluation of the effectiveness of the guidelines in Section 7 of the proposed revision to the Circular and recommendations for any changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide narrative evaluations of how Section 7 guidance assists standards management (e.g., FDA: guidelines sufficient, allow agency-specific tailoring, emphasize outcomes). Include recommended changes where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances when agency used government-unique standards instead of voluntary standards
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by P.L. 104-113, report when the agency used government-unique standards in lieu of voluntary consensus standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts and, implicitly, justifications (e.g., FDA reported 5 uses; others reported none). Where used, agencies should explain why voluntary standards were unavailable or inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency preference to adopt national/international consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Departmental/agency policy preference to adopt National Consensus Standards and other commercial and industry standards in preference to Federal/agency-specific standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies (e.g., DOE P251.1) explicitly state preference for adoption of voluntary standards and restrictions on mandated technical standards in rulemaking and orders. Use voluntary standards 'when appropriate' for work and hazards encountered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of performance-based rules permitting adoption of commercial standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Promulgation of 'performance-based' requirements (e.g., nuclear safety) which permit the adoption of commercial and industry standards as acceptable methods to implement the rules when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rules are performance-based, agencies may accept conformity to commercial/industry standards as acceptable methods. DOE P410.1A requires notice-and-comment rulemaking for new nuclear safety requirements and allows standards adoption as implementation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work Smart / necessary and sufficient standards selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: "Work Smart" (also called the 'necessary and sufficient' process) enabling contractors, with DOE approval, to identify and apply the set of standards that best fits their activities, focusing on outcomes and performance rather than prescriptive methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented through DOE processes and orders (e.g., P450.3, M450.3-1). Allows contractors to select voluntary consensus standards in-lieu-of DOE-developed standards subject to approval; demonstrated cost savings in pilots; intended to tailor standards to mission needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-year standards review cycle and conversion guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures establishing a five-year standards review cycle to check for continued applicability and guidance on conversion of Departmental standards to voluntary standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE TSPO procedures require five-year reviews and provide conversion guidance; agencies should maintain review cycles to ensure standards remain current and identify candidates for conversion to voluntary standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent third-party certification as evidence of safety/conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent (third party) certification to standards will be sufficient to demonstrate safety for the aspects of products/devices addressed by the standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDRH (FDA) example: third-party certification accepted where standards address safety aspects; agencies may rely on certification to reduce duplicative review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reviewers to utilize specific international standard series
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for agency reviewers to utilize the criteria contained in specific international standard series (e.g., IEC 601 series) in approval programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA made draft/final guidance available directing medical device reviewers to use IEC 601 criteria; agencies should document and communicate which standards reviewers should apply in regulatory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain searchable standards databases and tracking systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain databases to track standards activities and to provide reviewers with access to voluntary consensus standards (e.g., purchase of ROM/searchable databases from private vendors and standards development organizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: FDA purchased IHS and other standards databases; DOE TSPO maintains publications and electronic postings. Tracking supports reviewer access and reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards Policy Committee (SPC) governance and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency-level Standards Policy Committee (chaired by standards executive) to meet quarterly to review domestic and international standards issues, recommend agency-wide standards policy, oversee coordination and official participation, track/compile/report required information, and ensure appropriate standards review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPC structure (FDA example) centralizes policy, coordinates participation, and ensures reporting and review processes are followed. Liaison members on quality systems and environmental management strengthen expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in international harmonization activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Active participation in international harmonization efforts (e.g., ICH, WHO, Codex Alimentarius, ISO/IEC study groups) to harmonize regulatory requirements and technical guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies use harmonization to align domestic requirements with foreign governments, facilitate mutual recognition, and adopt international standards where appropriate; examples include FDA participation in ICH and WHO activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of voluntary standards except when none available or appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (e.g., FDA) utilize voluntary consensus standards except in cases when none are available or appropriate in meeting regulatory levels of protection (examples: food/color additives, pesticides, certain veterinary medicine products).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document exceptions and rationale when agency-specific or statutory protection levels require government-unique standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency obligation to consider national consensus standards in rulemaking/programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must consider the use of national consensus standards in their standards development programs (e.g., OSHA required under section 6(b)(8) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate consideration of existing consensus standards when developing regulations and cite standards used in final rules (OSHA example cites six ANSI standards in a final rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt/update regulatory references to reflect current standards designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Review and update regulatory references to standards to reflect current standards designations (e.g., FDA drafting proposed rules to amend regulations referencing out-of-date ASTM standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As standards are revised, agencies should update rule citations and references to preserve accuracy and relevance of regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of voluntary standards to promote environmental and energy efficiency objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and adoption of voluntary consensus standards for the purpose of promoting environmentally sound and energy-efficient materials, products, systems, services, or practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some agencies report adoption of standards that further environmental/energy goals (examples cited under DOJ and HUD reporting). Agencies should identify standards serving these policy objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish topical standards committees and technical liaisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize topical standards committees composed of subject matter experts as focal points for standards activities, review of counterpart voluntary standards, and development of Departmental/Federal positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE example: 12 topical committees recognized to coordinate review, address application issues, and develop positions. Use liaison members and contact groups (e.g., private laboratory issues) as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and convert candidate agency technical standards to voluntary standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Process to better define 'candidate' agency technical standards for conversion to voluntary standards and to work with voluntary standards organizations (e.g., ANSI-NSB) on conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE reported identifying specific candidate standards and engaging with ANSI-NSB; agencies should document candidate selection, conversion steps, and engage counterparts in the voluntary standards community.
